info.desc: Amnesiac is the fifth studio album by the English alternative rock band Radiohead. It was released on 4 June 2001 in the United Kingdom and on 5 June 2001 in the United States and Canada, debuting at #1 on the UK charts and #2 on the Billboard Top 200. Seen as the furthest departure yet from the rock style and heart-on-sleeve songwriting of the band's early career, Amnesiac nevertheless has more audible guitar than its direct predecessor Kid A, and unlike that album, it spun off several singles. Like Kid A, it synthesizes influences of electronic music, ambient music, classical .

podcast.body: Part of the "greatest creative explosion" era with `Kid A` and `Hail to the Thief`, this album's recording sessions were extensive and demanding, yielding thousands of hours of recordings. Thom Yorke later revisited discarded material from these sessions for his solo debut. "la mayor explosión creativa que tuvo Tom Jorken toda su vida fue la que grabó en la gran triilogía del quidad de la amnesia y de la emite y ron."

Radiohead's fifth album, released barely ten months after "Kid A." It originated from material recorded simultaneously with "Kid A" but was "saved and held back" from that album, rather than being "left over." "Amnesiac" is described as more conventional than "Kid A," featuring guitars, real drums, and more normal song structures. It also included recordings of songs that had become live favorites. Despite its conventional approach, some fans were left feeling unsatisfied, desiring a return to the style of "Okay Computer." "In other words, this new album was recorded pretty much simultaneously with Kid A but is designed to be taken separately."

podcast.body: This album is explicitly described as forming part of a creative trilogy alongside "Kid A" and another album referred to as "i-MIDB-ROM." While "Kid A" itself is not just an album but part of this larger creative output, "Amnesiac" is a direct continuation of the vast experimental material generated during the extensive "Kid A" recording sessions. "el quidá en la NESIA y el i-MIDB-ROM."
